summary: The PROMISE Act of 2026 establishes a formal process for the Social Security Advisory Board and Congress to review and act on the long-term solvency of the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund and the Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund. It mandates specific reporting, public listening sessions, and fast-track legislative procedures in the Senate and House of Representatives to consider and vote on bills aimed at achieving 50-year solvency for the trust funds.

affected_groups.effect: Must develop recommendations, hold public listening sessions, request public information, and submit a detailed report and proposed legislative language to Congress by September 14, 2026.
Subject to strict scheduling rules, mandatory convening provisions, limited debate hours (100 hours), and specific voting requirements to consider and vote on Social Security solvency legislation.
affected_groups.group: Members of Congress and Congressional Committees

affected_groups.effect: Required to provide technical assistance, suitable workspace, administrative support services, and security services to the Social Security Advisory Board upon request.
affected_groups.group: Federal Agencies (Architect of the Capitol, General Services Administration, and others)

key_provisions: Requires the Social Security Advisory Board to develop recommendations and legislative language to achieve long-term solvency (paying 100 percent of scheduled benefits for at least 50 years) and submit a report to Congress by September 14, 2026.
Requires the Social Security Advisory Board to hold public listening sessions and issue a public request for information regarding ways to achieve long-term solvency.

Establishes fast-track legislative procedures, including mandatory introduction of a Social Security bill by September 17, 2026, committee reporting deadlines of November 9, 2026, and strict limits on debate and amendments.

Sets specific requirements for substitute amendments in Congress, stipulating that they must be certified as achieving long-term solvency and must alter outlays, revenues, or financing related to Social Security or supplemental security income programs.
Requires a vote on passage of the Social Security bill in the Senate and House of Representatives, with the Senate requiring a three-fifths affirmative vote and the House requiring a majority vote.

Provides a decennial review process starting in calendar year 2037, triggered if the Social Security Board of Trustees finds the trust funds cannot pay 100 percent of scheduled benefits for a 50-year period.

It mandates specific reporting, public listening sessions, and fast-track legislative procedures in the Senate and House of Representatives to consider and vote on bills aimed at achieving 50-year solvency for the trust funds.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a specialized, time-sensitive legislative pipeline designed to force Congress to directly address the long-term financial solvency of the Social Security trust funds through expedited floor procedures and mandatory votes.
